teaser.text: Magna International is a global automotive supplier: it makes vehicle parts and systems, and sometimes engineers and assembles whole vehicles for automakers. The dollar that enters Magna begins with an automaker’s program and ends, after materials, people and factories are paid, as operating profit—or as a loss when the plan misses.

stock.title: Magna stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Magna's stock forecast weighs recovery scenarios, operating drivers, real cash flow and the valuation investors pay today.
stock.opening: Magna's weighted scenario is C$63.32 in October 2027, then C$94.60 in October 2029. It hinges on new programs ramping, Complete Vehicles utilization improving and recurring cash flow supporting investment and buybacks.
stock.closing: The full Magna memo also answers how Magna's business works, who its rivals are, how management is executing and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: Where could Magna's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is C$63.32 in October 2027. That is −29%, dividends included. It is C$78.45 in October 2028. The return is −10%. It reaches C$94.60 in October 2029. The return is +11%. The bear case has a 32% probability. The base case has 51%. The bull case has 17%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Magna?

paragraphs.text: The bear case gives $1,053 million first, then $1,250 million and $1,399 million. It reflects softer production, weak utilization and launch or tariff-recovery shortfalls. The bull case gives $1,801 million first, then $2,001 million and $2,198 million, requiring program ramps and margins above the historical average.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Magna really make?

paragraphs.text: Real free cash flow subtracts stock compensation from cash from operations less capital spending. It treats share awards as a cost to owners and gives a stricter view of cash left after investment. Free-cash-flow yield then compares that cash with the market value investors place on the shares.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Magna today?

paragraphs.text: At C$93.19 a share on October 17, 2026, investors are paying for Magna’s expected earnings recovery as well as its existing operations.

The sharp difference between Magna’s trailing and forward P/E makes the forecast especially important. Trailing P/E uses earnings already reported, while forward P/E uses expected earnings. If a share costs $100 and last year’s earnings were $4 per share, the trailing P/E would be 25 times; if next year’s expected earnings were $10, the forward P/E would be 10 times. The gap is therefore a forecast of recovery, not a mathematical error.

dividend.title: Magna dividend
dividend.meta_description: Magna's dividend history, cash coverage, plans, and current yield are explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: Magna pays $2.06 per share in the base case, rising to $2.14 and then $2.22 by October 2029. Magna's 2025 cash generation funded fixed assets, investments, debt repayment, retained cash, and shareholder payouts, while buybacks also competed for cash.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Magna's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Magna pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $2.06 per share to $2.14. It reaches $2.22 by October 2029. The bear case holds it at $1.98 before a small recovery to $2.00, while the bull case reaches $2.34. The company has raised dividends for sixteen consecutive years, but gives no numerical growth target.

blocks.heading: Is Magna's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The pattern looked more conservative in 2025. Magna generated $3.598 billion from operating activities, spent $1.313 billion on fixed assets, and used another $499 million for investments, other assets, and intangible assets. It also repaid debt. Much of the cash was therefore retained, reinvested, or used to strengthen the balance sheet rather than distributed.

Magna then accelerated repurchases in 2026. The board authorized purchases of up to 25.3 million shares. In the first half of 2026, Magna bought 15.0 million shares for $905 million and planned to buy the remaining approximately 9 million shares in the second half. Buybacks can raise earnings per share if earnings hold up, but they compete with debt reduction, factories, and acquisitions for cash.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to US$41.3–42.5 billion in sales. It targets a 6.3%–6.6% adjusted EBIT margin. Adjusted EPS guidance is US$6.70–7.30. Free cash flow guidance is US$1.75–1.85 billion. The test is whether productivity and efficiency sustain margins after tariff and EV-program recoveries fade.

blocks.heading: What were Magna’s last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Q1 2026 offers a useful contrast because held-for-sale impairment charges affected reported income before income taxes and net income. Q2 cash was also strong, but first-half cash included customer recoveries. The specialist therefore asks whether margins and cash conversion persist in later quarters.

blocks.heading: What should Magna watch on October 30, 2026?

paragraphs.text: The outcome turns on new programs ramping, Complete Vehicles utilization improving and recurring cash flow supporting investment and buybacks. Q3 results on October 30, 2026, will test margins, cash flow and recovery against guidance. The repurchase authorization expires November 6, 2026, while buybacks compete with investment and debt reduction for cash. Investor Day on November 11, 2026, centers on margins, investment, returns and time to scale for the non-automotive strategy.
